newsitem.title: UK: UK government survives vital vote on Europe.
newsitem.headline: UK government survives vital vote on Europe.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major's battered government survived a crucial parliamentary challenge over the European Union on Monday night.

The opposition Labour Party bid to defeat the Conservative government in a vote on the EU's fishing policy was rejected by 316 votes to 305. This was the government's first real test of unity since it lost its overall majority in the House of Commons last week.
The Labour Party had said earlier it was considering putting down a confidence motion if the government lost.

Major was defeated by two votes in a similar vote a year ago and soldiered on. Since then the Conservative Party's position in parliament has worsened because of defections and by-election losses. Opinion polls give Labour a lead of around 20 points.
But a vital group of Ulster Unionist MPs from Northern Ireland swung behind the government on Monday night after receiving assurances of help for the fishermen of the province.

The Conservatives are deeply split on the EU. Major has said he wants to keep going in government until May, close to the deadline for calling an election. But with just 323 parliamentary seats, level with the combined opposition, any slip could force an early election.
